title: Learn English Faster With These 5 Mind-Freeing Games

lines.text: You are 75% more likely to remember
something when it's fun and that means
faster fluency. So here are five fluency
games to free your mind. Game one, the
word chain. Why this game? Word chain
builds fast thinking and fluent
speaking. It forces you to find words
quickly without translating them, just
like real life conversation. How to
play? Say the first word that pops into
your head. So for
example, doodle. The last letter of
doodle is E. That is the first letter of
my next
word.
English. Again, the last letter here is
H. That's the first letter of my next
word, which will be
haaloo. Keep going for 1 minute without
stopping. Here's my example starting
with mug. Mug. Grow. Water. Rain. Nut.
Terrain. Never. Reed. Draw. Wigwam.
Muster. Rembrandt. Tiger. Rhino.
Octopus. Snake.
Elephant.
Twitch.
Hack. By the end. I slowed down, but
that's okay. Keep going. Game two, topic
pop. Why this game? Topic pop sharpens
your vocabulary around one idea. It
trains your brain to organize words fast
and speak with more depth and detail.
How to play? Pick a topic like animals
or food and say as many words as you can
in one minute. And if you want to track
your progress and get even better, you
can keep a simple tally. So here's my
example. The topic is animals. Here we
go. Rhino, rabbit, horse, duck, donkey,
dog, doberman, rat,
mouse, goldfish, capibara, tapia, zebra,
elephant. Here are some scores to aim
for. Beginner 0 to 10. Intermediate 11
to 20. Experts 21 plus. Each time you
play, try to aim a little higher. Just
like doing one more rep in the gym, your
brain will get stronger, faster, and
more fluent. Game three, letter magic.
Why this game? Letter magic gets you
speaking out loud again and again. It
fine-tunes your pronunciation. It
strengthens your mouth muscles and it
builds smoother, faster speech. How to
play? Choose any letter from the
alphabet. I'm going to choose letter G.
Then name as many words as you can that
begin with your letter in one minute.
Here's my example. Gobbled, green, grow,
grass, give, gay, gas, gunk, grip, grim.
Just like in the topic pop game, here
are the scores to aim for. Beginner 0 to
10. Intermediate 11 to 20. Experts 21
plus. Bonus tip for this game. Once you
finished, take a dictionary or an online
dictionary and go to your letter. So,
I'm going to letter G. Find 10 new words
that you have never seen before. 10
interesting words, 10 funny words, any
words that you choose. and write them
down. This step is important. When you
write something down, it lodges in your
memory. Write the words down. Put them
in example sentences and try relate the
words to something personal for you.
Here's a fun example. I found the word
gullible. Gullible means too willing to
believe or accept what other people tell
you and therefore easily tricked. I can
relate this to a personal experience. My
dad when I was young used to say, "Look
up. Gullibles on the ceiling. I would
look up and he would laugh at me." Now
that I've related that word to a
personal memory of mine, I'm way more
likely to remember it. You can use this
for any vocabulary. After you've
collected your 10 words, you're going to
play this game again. Speak for one more
minute and try to remember as many of
the words that you have just learned so
you can add these to your active
vocabulary. Game four. What what word
flow? Why this game? Have you ever had
that moment where someone asks you
something and you can't think of
anything to say? Yeah, me too. Word flow
is a fun solution. It helps you think
freely in English without overthinking.
It boosts your fluency, creativity, and
confidence all at the same time. How to
play? Look at something around you, like
a speaker. Then say the first word that
pops into your head. From that word, say
another word that relates to it. And if
you don't understand that, here's an
example. Speaker, music, Beethoven,
Mozart, composer, orchestra, violin,
cello, strings, guitar, tune, song,
musician, Ed Sheeran, pop, balloon, pin,
sharp, knife, scissors, cut, paper,
wood, tree, forest, orangutan,
Indonesia, India, curry, spice, chili,
cold, freezing, biff, slang, language,
linguist, dictionary, and so on. Bonus
tip to make this game way more fun, you
can play with a partner, a friend, or
someone who just loves language, words,
and creativity. So, let me ask my
girlfriend if she wants to play. Jang.
Yeah. Do you want to play a game? Not
really. Oh, well, she's busy. Moving on.
Game five. Random Jump. Why this game?
Random jump trains you to switch topics
fast. It prepares you for real
conversations where ideas bounce around.
How to play? Jump from word to word with
no easy connections allowed. This one is
a real challenge to stretch your
creativity and quick thinking. This one
is hard for me, too. So, I'm going to
start slowly. Here's my example.
Baby,
Skyscraper,
Carrot,
Slingshot,
Habadasherie, Minion,
Omegle,
Paper,
Ominous, Spend. Terrific. A bonus tip
for all of these games
is to have fun. Having fun triggers
dopamine in your brain, which helps you
remember up to 30% more effectively. So,
have fun, enjoy these games, and let me
know in the comments which one that
you're going to try. You can also
download the free PDF I've attached with
this video, and it goes through all the
games in more detail with plenty of
examples. If you found this video
useful, make sure to like, subscribe,
and share it with a friend. Thank you.
Big love and happy learning. Peace.
